title: Chiral-Structured Superconductors TrX4 (Tr = Rh, Ir; X = Ge, Si): A Platform for Mixed-Parity Pairing and Topological States
authors: Zhenhai Yu, Yunguan Ye, Yuwei Zhou, Chaoyang Chu, Congcong Le, Lin Wu, Jian Yuan, Tong Shi, Qingxin Dong, Jinggeng Zhao, Wei Xia, Xiangqi Liu, Xia Wang, Bosen Wang, Jinguang Cheng, Yanhang Ma, Xianxin Wu, Xiangang Wan, Huiqiu Yuan, Yanfeng Guo
abstract: Chiral-structured superconductors, with simultaneous broken mirror and inversion symmetries, promote unconventional superconductivity through parity-mixing mechanisms. Yet a few bulk chiral-structured superconductors are known, partly due to the difficulty in directly determining their atomic-scale chirality. Here we report three chiral-structured superconductors, , RhGe4, IrGe4, and IrSi4, synthesized under high pressure, with Tc values of about 1.6 K, 1.1 K, and 2.5 K, respectively.Using atomic resolution Cs-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) combined with X-ray diffraction characterizations, we directly confirm their chiral structure (space group P3121). This real space imaging approach overcomes ambiguities in traditional diffraction based methods. These materials exhibit type-II superconductivity, and the enhancement of spin-orbit coupling (SOC) leads to the emergence of mixed parity pairing. Calculations also reveal symmetry protected Weyl points near the Fermi level, which is robust against the SOC. Our work not only expands the family of chiral-structured superconductors but also demonstrates the indispensable role of STEM in directly determining chiral crystal structures. These materials thus offer a clean platform to explore the interplay among structural chirality, SOC, mixed parity superconductivity, and topological quantum phenomena.
summary: This work reports on three novel chiral-structured superconductors ($	ext{RhGe}_4$, $	ext{IrGe}_4$, $	ext{IrSi}_4$), using advanced STEM to confirm their unique crystal structure. The research establishes these materials as a platform where structural chirality and strong SOC induce mixed-parity superconductivity, alongside predicted topological Weyl points.
main_problem: The research aims to explore the complex interplay between structural chirality, strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC), mixed-parity superconductivity, and topological quantum phenomena in novel superconducting materials.
main_result: The authors successfully synthesized and characterized three chiral superconductors ($	ext{RhGe}_4$, $	ext{IrGe}_4$, and $	ext{IrSi}_4$), confirming their structure using STEM and demonstrating evidence for mixed-parity pairing and symmetry-protected Weyl points.
method: The study combines high-pressure synthesis, advanced structural characterization (atomic-resolution STEM), detailed superconducting measurements ($ho(T)$, $M(T)$, specific heat), and first-principles electronic structure calculations.
model_or_system: The physical system consists of chiral-structured superconductors $	ext{TrX}_4$ ($	ext{RhGe}_4$, $	ext{IrGe}_4$, $	ext{IrSi}_4$), which possess broken mirror and inversion symmetries, leading to unconventional pairing mechanisms.
key_observables: Superconducting critical temperatures ($T_c \approx 1.1-2.6 	ext{ K}$), magnetic penetration depth ($\lambda(T)$), specific heat jump ($\Delta C/T$), and the presence of Weyl points in electronic structure calculations.
important_parameters: The enhancement of SOC is a key parameter driving mixed parity pairing; structural chirality ($P3_121$ space group) dictates the superconducting behavior.
main_assumptions: Traditional diffraction methods are insufficient for unambiguous chiral assignment, necessitating real-space STEM imaging. Superconductivity analysis relies on fitting specific heat and penetration depth data to various gap models (s-wave, p-wave, etc.).
figures_summary: Figures detail structural motifs, layered arrangements, temperature dependence of resistivity and magnetization curves, and analyses comparing superconducting gap fits from different symmetry models.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure moving from material synthesis and definitive chiral structure confirmation (STEM) to detailed measurements of superconducting properties ($ho(T)$, $M(T)$), followed by theoretical analysis using specific heat and penetration depth data to constrain the pairing symmetry.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter superconductivity, the explicit link between structural chirality, broken symmetries, and topological features (Weyl points) provides a rich platform for understanding emergent quantum states that could be relevant in engineered superconducting circuits or topological quantum computing architectures.
